Ahmad Hassan. Lloyds Banking Group, June 2025 to June 2026.

Two rotations in two Chief Controls Offices. My team won Emerging Tech Pioneers and I pitched it to the Group COO and CTO. In June I was not put forward for the graduate programme. That is here too.

  • 1stEmerging Tech Pioneers, from 70+ applicants

2Where I worked

Context

How Consumer Lending earns, and where a controls office fits.

Consumer Lending lends to personal customers: cards, loans, car finance, mortgages. Most income is interest; the risk is often operational: a process that harms customers, a supplier that fails.

Accelerate 2030 targets cost-to-income below 45%; pages 4 and 5 serve that.

Learned

I knew my tasks better than the business.

Next time

Learn how the business earns in month one.

3Finding my feet

From June 2025

A sixteen-person incident team, then my first project inside it.

My part

  • A call with every colleague in month one
  • Owned the playbooks used in live incidents
  • Led the SharePoint merge: survey, four general managers’ sign-off, build, trial

Impact

One place to look in a live incident.

Learned

New and without authority, I got sign-off first. Again on page 8.

Next time

Log my deliverables from week one.

4Paper to digital

2025

Every product against the Group’s paper-reduction targets.

My part

  • Led Printing & Mail after a supplier failed to deliver the bank’s post
  • Gathered data from every product area, some led by directors
  • Presented to the Managing Director of the Chief Controls Office

Impact

Every product against target, on one page.

Learned

Senior people want the conclusion first. Again on pages 5 and 7.

Next time

Share the tracker with each product area.

5The spike

Late 2025

Why supplier incidents doubled, and learning to ask for help.

My part

  • Co-owned the Power BI dashboard; automated its refresh
  • Pulled ServiceNow records into Excel datasets
  • Traced the doubling to a card-scheme migration; presented a pack to the COO director

Impact

One cause to fix, not many incidents to chase.

Learned

Asking early protects the deadline. Again on page 7.

Next time

Raise the first blocker within a day.

6The pitch

2025 to April 2026

Eight weeks from nothing to a winning proposition: tokenised farmland that keeps farms in the family.

My part

  • One of three placement students among 27
  • Business Lead. Learned tokenisation from experts; fitted overseas models to UK farmland
  • Customer insight via Aspire sessions; research into the Group’s farming commitments
  • A Sora 2 film of UK farmers

Impact

First place. Pitched to the Group COO and CTO; prototype approved by the Scottish Widows CEO.

Learned

Customers first gave the technology a problem to solve. Again on page 9.

Next time

Test the idea against policy change: December’s relief rise shrank the need.

7Decision-ready

January to June 2026

A new office. Clearer risk information, and a way past a reporting limit.

My part

  • Indicator Working Group: keep, fix or retire 1,200+ indicators
  • Checked Homes control labels; recommended corrections
  • Owned each product’s IT systems risk profile; presented it to risk owners
  • Noticed OpenPages fields the reports hid; got a platform-team call via a graduate I had met once

Impact

Risks judged on accurate information; a reporting gap put to its owners.

Learned

Speed beats polish when facts change daily. Answers often sit with strangers. Again on page 10.

Next time

Record my retire arguments; write a proposal before any call.

8Leading without a title

December 2025 to April 2026

Leading people who didn’t report to me.

My part

  • Aspire hub lead: ran the IP swap for 30+ students, then brought it into my second office
  • Brand ambassador at the Crisis hackathon, linking team and organisers
  • Ran my first team’s Christmas meeting, awards included

Impact

Thirty students saw another part of the Group.

Learned

People follow a clear plan and a reason to care.

Next time

Survey the swap afterwards.

9Strong scores, then a setback

2025 to 2026

Four quarterly reviews, then the Reflection Day.

Six of seven at 1 by June. Then the Reflection Day, where I was not put forward.

Learned

Good in the room isn’t telling my story. Again on page 10.

Next time

Prepare around my impact and the numbers behind it.
